name: United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (2026-2030)

children.name: By 2030, all people living in Malaysia, particularly those in vulnerable situations, have access to high-quality, rights-based, gender-responsive, and disability-inclusive social services.
children.description: The outcome statement for SPA 1 centres on inclusive social development and well-being. This is defined by equitable access to quality social services and the realization of basic human capabilities, as outlined in the relevant SDGs and international human rights instruments. Key dimensions include education, health, social protection, and food and nutrition, with the aim of enabling all people living in Malaysia to realise their full human potentials.

children.name: Access to inclusive quality and values-based education is improved for all children and young people.
children.description: This collaborative output addresses two interrelated challenges: gaps in mainstream education, including concerns about quality of attainment and increasing social polarization, and the difficulties faced by some non-citizen children in accessing schooling. This latter group includes undocumented and stateless children (particularly in Sabah) as well as refugees, where civil society and the UN often play a critical role in service provision. These educational disparities have far-reaching implications, given the central role of human capital development in national economic transformation and the importance of education in the socialization of values and promotion of social cohesion.

agencies.name: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees

children.name: The healthcare system is more resilient and better capacitated to deliver universal access to care, promote well-being and healthy ageing, and address population-specific risk factors.
children.description: This collaborative output supports both the strengthening of national health systems and their ability to deliver equitable, quality care across the life cycle for all communities. UN agencies will align their work with Malaysia’s Health White Paper (2023), focusing on the development of a health system that is adequately financed, equitable and affordable. The UN will contribute to system resilience by supporting infrastructure, service continuity and fiscal strategies that balance public health financing with reduced out of pocket costs. Informed by the lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic, the UN will also assist in building preparedness capacities for future public health emergencies.

agencies.name: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees

children.name: The social protection system is strengthened to provide universal coverage throughout the lifecycle, especially for people in vulnerable situations.
children.description: Malaysia’s social protection system faces two primary challenges: incomplete lifecycle coverage for the general population and inadequate provision for individuals with heightened or overlapping vulnerabilities, such as men and women with disabilities, children, older persons, and people living in poverty. These gaps reduce the system’s capacity to mitigate risks and shocks, enable equitable access and effectively address fragmentation, thereby weakening human capital, limiting inclusive economic growth, and contributing to intergenerational cycles of disadvantage, with adverse impacts on nutrition, health, and well-being.  Malaysia is well-positioned to embrace a progressive universality model in strengthening its Social Protection Floor (SPF), to ensure that all citizens, particularly the most vulnerable populations, have access to essential benefits that secure their fundamental rights to health, income, and well-being.

children.name: Food and nutrition systems meet the needs of all people in Malaysia, address undernutrition and obesity, specifically among women, children, and other vulnerable groups.
children.description:
Malaysia faces a triple burden of malnutrition challenge with the coexistence of undernutrition and stunting, especially among children, alongside rising rates of obesity and micronutrient deficiency. These trends reflect both structural inequities and changing consumption patterns linked to rapid economic growth and urbanization. The burden is not evenly distributed, with significant disparities across geographic regions and population groups, requiring disaggregated, equity-sensitive approaches. 
In response, the UN will support the development of integrated, sustainable, and locally adapted food and nutrition systems and policies. Interventions will promote access to sufficient, affordable, and nutritious food while addressing behavioural, cultural and socioeconomic determinants of poor diets. The UN will also contribute to strengthening national capacities in food systems governance, nutrition-sensitive agriculture, and multi-sector coordination.

framework.name: Economic Transformation for Inclusive and Sustainable Prosperity

children.name: By 2030, Malaysia’s economy is resilient, environmentally sustainable, and delivers growth and opportunities for all, leveraging the contributions of women, youth, and people in lagging regions.
children.description: The outcome statement for SPA 2 focuses on inclusive and sustainable economic transformation. It envisions a high-income economy that is future-ready, resilient and environmentally sustainable, driving broad-based growth and enabling opportunities for all, particularly, women, youth and populations in lagging regions. Economic transformation is approached not only in terms of growth maximization, but of structural change that enhances equity, sustainability and productivity in high value-added sectors focused on technology but also including high-value service industries (notably tourism). This includes diversifying the economy through innovation and digitalization by leveraging the Malaysia Digital initiatives to promote the growth of these digital industries, facilitating a green transition, helping to create decent jobs and more functional labour market and expanding economic participation and opportunity via targeted investments.

children.name: The labour market provides demand-driven opportunities, enhances women’s economic participation, enables reskilling and upskilling, and protects rights for all with a focus on caregivers, migrant workers, persons with disabilities, youth, and women.
children.description:
Recognizing the central role of employment in driving inclusive growth, this output supports efforts to address persistent labour market disparities and barriers to decent work. Particular attention is given to the economic participation of women, whose labour force participation continues to lag significantly behind, as well as to groups which are disadvantaged in the labour market. 
UN programming and advocacy will promote gender-responsive labour policies and workplace rights, while supporting the development of a more inclusive and demand-driven skills economy.  This includes strengthening the TVET architecture, ensuing that it is better aligned with the evolving needs of industry, and closing skills gaps, particularly in digital, green, and new technologies. A core focus will be on enhancing productivity and enabling access to higher-value employment for women and youth. 
To advance broader inclusion and equity, UN interventions will support the creation of enabling work environments for persons with disabilities, as well as address the employment challenges faced by informal sector workers and migrants. In addition, the UN will also address systemic drivers of child labour in specific sectors. Environmental sustainability will be promoted as an integral part of this transition, including efforts to green the workplace and mainstream just transition principles across labour market reforms.

agencies.name: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees

children.name: Productivity and competitiveness, particularly of MSMEs, are enhanced as Malaysia transitions to a digital and green high-income economy with a fair and transparent business environment which promotes SDG-aligned investments
children.description:
Malaysia’s productivity growth and competitiveness, especially among micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) remain constrained by structural and capacity-related challenges. This output focuses on addressing these constraints through targeted support to enhance enterprise performance, enabling broader economic transformation. Interventions will include improved technology transfer, labour reskilling, and better access to finance and trade opportunities. The explicit linking of productivity and competitiveness gains with greener and more inclusive business models will be a dimension of the UN’s approach. 
The UN will seek to deliver this, by supporting the take-up of ESG practices and investments particularly by MSMEs and securing wider SDG compliance via the realignment of business incentives, in particular in the context of the forthcoming National ESG Strategic Plan, a ten-year plan envisioned to take Malaysian business entities beyond ESG compliance, and drive competitive advantage. In the social and governance spheres, this includes the business and human rights agenda, and in the environmental sphere, improving resource and energy efficiency, and facilitating access to new technologies and markets, such as those related to electric vehicles, renewable energy, and artificial intelligence. 

To enable these shifts, the UN will provide technical support for policy reforms aimed at creating a more supportive operating environment, including appropriate incentive structures to encourage improvements in productivity and competitiveness alongside SDG objectives. This involves supporting and accelerating current government reforms and tackling key bottlenecks, particularly to MSME expansion, notably, access to finance and trade opportunities for all sectors, including agri-commodities. The UN’s work will also include supporting the scaling up of (this is as mentioned in RMK13) MSMEs, particularly to access green financing, foster sustainable business practices and enable their integration into global green supply chains.

agencies.name: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation

children.name: Infrastructures and investments are more equitable, recognizing the needs of urban and rural areas, and communities at risk of being left behind.
children.description:
Spatial and group-based inequalities, such as between urban and rural areas, core, and peripheral regions and vis a vis groups at risk of being left behind, remain among Malaysia’s most pressing development challenges. Some 75 per cent of the population live in cities, and there is growing urban sprawl and urban-rural gaps.  These disparities undermine inclusive growth and risk constraining the country’s HIC transition. While Government’s efforts are underway to address these imbalances, a more data-driven, inclusive, and spatially sensitive approach is required to ensure more equitable development outcomes. 
In response, the UN will support efforts to strengthen national and subnational data systems and analytical capacities to better identify and track geographic and demographic disparities.  This evidence base will inform more responsive and inclusive policymaking, particularly in relation to infrastructure development, service provision, and public investment. These efforts are especially pertinent to regional and local planning initiatives, addressing spatial disparities.
Indeed, complementing this, the UN programming will promote and enable greater investments in underserved regions and for vulnerable populations. This includes supporting initiatives to reduce rural-urban divides, address disparities between Malaysia’s core and lagging states, and help enhance infrastructure provision and services to groups at risk of being left behind.

children.name: By 2030, natural resources are managed sustainably, biodiversity is preserved, pollution is reduced, and climate action is enhanced towards delivering greater resilience and national climate change commitments
children.description: This outcome addresses the in-country impacts of the triple planetary crisis (climate change, biodiversity loss and pollution). It reflects growing vulnerabilities of Malaysia’s natural environment to extreme weather events, and rising temperatures and sea levels. These risks are driven by global environmental dynamics and intensified by Malaysia’s rapid economic trajectory, increasing energy needs, growing consumption, and continued fossil fuel dependence.

children.name: Malaysia adopts just, clean energy, low-carbon, gender-responsive and circular economy solutions, including more effectively managed waste and improved regulation of pollution.
children.description:
This collaborative output addresses both policy formulation and implementation of Malaysia’s green transition. At the policy level, UN support will focus on enhancing climate mitigation and adaptation strategies through the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) framework and national adaptation planning. Particular attention will be given to addressing plastic pollution, particularly within marine areas, and reversing biodiversity loss in vulnerable localities.  
At the operational level, the UN will provide technical assistance on the roll-out of clean energy, low-carbon and just transition policies, as well as policies related to waste management and pollution control. These will include the adoption of climate-adaptive technologies, application of circular economy models, and improved environmental planning and regulation at subnational levels across all sectors. 
Additionally, industry-level efforts will focus on high-impact sectors, such as renewable energy, energy efficiency, and electric mobility, while embedding just transition principles to protect workers and communities affected by the ongoing shifts in energy production and consumption.  The UN will advocate for improved environmental stewardship across enterprises, including MSMEs, by promoting low-carbon practices, ESG-aligned investments, and circular economy solutions.

children.name: Institutions are strengthened and local communities, particularly indigenous peoples, are empowered to drive sustainable, gender-responsive and inclusive natural resource and biodiversity management, and nature-based solutions.
children.description:
This output focuses on enhancing institutional capacity and community empowerment to support effective and equitable environmental stewardship. At the federal level, the UN will provide technical assistance to strengthen leadership, coordination, and policy implementation on urban environmental management. At the subnational level, support will be tailored to specific needs of local governments, including improving spatial planning and delivering tailored local solutions related to waste management, air quality and urban living conditions, including the preservation and provision of green spaces.
UN programming will contribute to systems strengthening and building the capacities of institutions to decarbonize, restore and protect eco-systems, and promote disaster resilience through risk-assessment and risk-proofing of infrastructure and investments. This will include strengthening of climate data for evidence-informed decision-making and environmental governance. Special emphasis will be on building the capacity of local governments to manage municipal, chemical and biomedical waste, improve the urban environment and living conditions, and integrate pollution-related risks into local public health frameworks. 
The UN will also work with the Government to leverage global and regional climate and biodiversity knowledge through inter-governmental exchange and South-South cooperation. Cross-border environmental challenges such as haze pollution, waste trafficking, and marine pollution caused by disposal of plastic debris in the ocean will be also addressed in partnerships with national and regional stakeholders.
Finally, UN agencies will seek to protect the rights of the resource-dependent communities, including indigenous peoples and local communities, promoting equitable and sustainable access to natural resources, ensuring adherence to Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) standards. The UN will also explore and leverage the potential of traditional knowledge systems to deliver better environmental and resource management at the local level.

agencies.name: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation

children.name: Resilience of communities, women and children, and other groups most vulnerable to environmental hazards, shocks, and disasters, is strengthened by enhancing adaptive capacities and meaningful participation in decision-making and solutions.
children.description:
At both the strategic and operational levels, the UN will support policy and programming measures that promote greater resilience to environmental and climate-related shocks to all communities. This will include enabling policy development at the federal and state levels to advance climate-adaptive investments, strengthened climate-resilient social services and to facilitate and incentivize the building of resilience within society more broadly. UN interventions will include assisting with the adoption of new techniques within government (risk-assessment/risk proofing) and applying fiscal and regulatory instruments to manage and mitigate environmental risks. The UN will seek to enable effective coordination across levels of government and across localities, recognizing the variability of threats and vulnerabilities. 
Through partnerships with civil society, the UN will reach out to local communities to engage them in greening workplace and household practices and promoting locally tailored measures to mitigate shocks and enhance self-adaptation. Special attention will be given to the differentiated vulnerabilities of the groups most at risk, especially women, low-income households, and those facing multiple forms of exclusion. Targeted support will also focus on communities in vulnerable and geographically remote areas, including indigenous peoples and those which are resource-dependent (e.g., fishing communities).

framework.name: Governance, Participation, Rights and Social Cohesion

children.name: By 2030, all people in Malaysia enjoy human rights and live in a safe, inclusive, and cohesive society, supported by accountable and transparent public institutions which ensure coordinated, evidence-based and participatory policymaking.
children.description: This outcome focuses on strengthening governance systems and institutional capacities in line with the international human rights standards and normative frameworks. It reflects the Government’s overarching emphasis, as articulated in the Thirteenth Plan, on institutional reform as a core pillar of Malaysia’s development pathway and its forthcoming HIC transition. In this context, UN support aims to help Malaysia embed and uphold global standards of peace and security, the rule of law, human rights, transparency and accountability across all levels of governance, including as part of the efforts to ensure the achievement of the SDG targets by 2030.

children.name: People, especially women and children, benefit from justice and human rights protections as institutions and legal frameworks are aligned with international normative standards and function effectively.
children.description:
The UN will leverage its normative mandate to advocate for the realization of human rights for all, with a focus on vulnerable groups . Efforts will include advocacy for Malaysia’s accession to the six-core international human rights treaties not yet ratified, and for the reduction of reservations on the three ratified treaties (CEDAW, CRC and CRPD). UNCT will promote women’s participation in social, economic, and political life, advocate against practices that harm women and girls, and support mainstreaming of gender equality and women’s empowerment in development plans and M&E frameworks. The UN will also support the implementation of existing international commitments and obligations on women, peace and security.
Through partnerships with the private sector, the UN will promote human rights in the workplace and in the provision of goods and services, building on the work already underway during the previous CF cycle.  Complementary efforts will support the endorsement and implementation of ILO labour conventions, ensuring alignment with international labour standards.

agencies.name: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees

children.name: Institutions and participatory mechanisms are strengthened to effectively promote inclusion and social cohesion and respond to all forms of violence (including gender-based violence), crime, exploitation, stigmatization, discrimination, and harmful practices.
children.description:
Recognizing the Government’s strong commitment to social harmony and national unity, the UN will contribute to the implementation of the National Unity Policy and Blueprint 2021-2030 to strengthen inter-ethnic relations, social cohesion, and trust by engaging with diverse communities and promoting interactions and exchange. Programming will support dialogue and promote innovative channels for direct engagement, with particular emphasis on women, youth, and persons with disabilities, ensuring their meaningful participation and representation at all levels of decision-making and governance. 
The UN will also partner with media and civil society stakeholders to promote digital citizenship and media literacy, to counter divisive narratives, xenophobia, hate speech and misogyny and to combat discrimination and stigma.  Interventions will also seek to strengthen multisectoral responses to prevent and respond to violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, children, and persons with disabilities.
UN agencies will continue to advocate for the rights and protection of refugees, stateless people, and undocumented populations, including tailored support to mitigate stigma and exclusion. Specific attention will be given to migrant workers, including advocacy on rights, welfare, and access to services and remedies. Given the scale of the challenge, particular focus will be placed on Sabah, where a significant share of the stateless and undocumented population resides, to support durable policy responses.

children.name: Institutions are more accountable, transparent and gender-responsive, implement innovative evidence-based policies and laws at national and subnational levels, and prevent and combat corruption and transnational crime.
children.description:
The UN will support efforts to enhance institutional accountability, transparency, and responsiveness at all levels of government. This will include promoting international benchmarking, peer learning, and the adaptation of innovative governance approaches. The UN will advocate for strengthening of state and local government capacities to enhance service delivery and local development. This will be complemented by in-situ programming, particularly in urban areas, and SDG-based local planning, budgeting, and implementation monitoring. This will be enhanced by UN support to national authorities, including the Department of Statistics of Malaysia (DOSM), in generating, accessing, and utilizing SDG-related and other data, disaggregated by group characteristics (specifically including gender) and locality, to strengthen evidenced-based policymaking. National evaluation capacities will also be strengthened.
Support to anti-corruption efforts will include both prevention and effective enforcement of laws. The UN will promote innovative approaches harnessing digitalization and new technologies, open budgeting initiatives, while also advancing traditional accountability mechanisms such as the right to information, public reporting of corruption, and whistle-blower protections.
The UN system will also contribute to efficient, resilient, and inclusive delivery of public services by enabling digital governance through capacity building, and the transfer of technology and know- how. UN agencies will support law enforcement, including enhancing cross-border cooperation on cybercrime investigation and intelligence sharing among law enforcement agencies, as well as provide recommendations for policy development, to prevent, and counter organized and transnational crime, including trafficking in persons, smuggling of drugs, cybercrime, scamming operations and illicit financial flows.

projects.description: Malaysia’s SDG Roadmap Phase III (Roadmap) will ultimately serve as a testament to the country’s commitment to an equitable, sustainable and inclusive future as it pursues the 2030 Agenda in alignment with Malaysia MADANI Framework. As the main policy document guiding the nation’s last 5-year journey towards the 2030 Agenda, this Roadmap provides a blueprint for accelerated SDG implementation. It articulates specific indicator targets, means of implementation and accelerators tailored to translating global aspirations into actionable national steps, along with methods for monitoring and evaluating performance. Malaysia is dedicated to empowering state governments, local authorities and communities, fostering ownership and participation in the localising SDG initiatives. The Roadmap will take into consideration the policy, institutional or implementation gaps that may hinder the progress of the SDGs and national targets as laid out in the Ekonomi MADANI Framework and Thirteenth Malaysia Plan.

projects.name: Enhancing access of refugees to labour mobility pathways through skills development
projects.description: The project seeks to establish a pilot to address the barriers faced by refugees in Malaysia in accessing labor migration opportunities. This initiative will empower refugees by equipping them with the necessary skills required for migration pathways to a destination country (tentatively Australia). In collaboration with a local training centre in Malaysia, the project will provide demand-driven training aligned with labour market needs in industrial sectors abroad. In its initial phase, the project will gather data to understand existing barriers and identify opportunities for labour migration from Malaysia to target destination countries. The project aims to create a pilot labour mobility pathway with one country, which will serve as a model for future inclusion of other countries. The project will be implemented under the Malaysia-UN SDG Trust Fund as a joint program between IOM and UNIDO. As lead agency, IOM will drive coordination efforts and work closely with refugee communities in Malaysia to identify beneficiaries and support their access to migration pathways. UNIDO will focus on providing demand-driven skills development through a local pilot training centre, ensuring that training is aligned with the labour market needs of the destination. projects.description: The UN Women Gender Action Lab: Innovation and Impact for Gender Equality in Asia-Pacific, powered by the Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPs) is a dynamic action platform launched by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade of the Government of Australia and UN Women in Asia and the Pacific. GAL will be launched for an initial a period of four years (March 2024-March 20248) with a particular focus on Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines, and with activities for the broader ASEAN region. Gender Action Lab (GAL) is envisioned to grow in a long-term, multi-stakeholder and multi-donor platform across Asia and the Pacific, seeking to galvanize efforts for gender-transformative action and impact in the private sector and leveraging its innovation capabilities to advance gender equality, women’s empowerment and sustainable development to build a more inclusive economies in the region. In Malaysia, GAL implements the WEPs Corporate Action Lab and engages stakeholders for the Asia-Pacific Sustainable Finance Lab (a GAL ‘systems’ lab operating at regional level).

projects.name: Strengthening Climate Resilience and food security through South-South Cooperation in adaptive rice production in Malaysia (and the Philippines)
projects.description: Preparatory Assistance for a project of which main objectives are to address the climate threat to food security. The specific objectives are # i) support marginalized rice farmer communities in Malaysia and the Philippines through enhanced extension services; ii) enhance rice farmer#s adaptation capacity through community-level agricultural climate adaptation plans implemented at community level by empowering local leadership in pursuing effective action on climate change adaptation following the Local-led adaptation principles of access and equity.; iii) develop socially inclusive localized adaption strategies by ensuring clear expectations between implementing entities and local partners, building trust with marginalized and vulnerable farmers group, involving local government and sensitization on locally-led approaches ; and iv) create an enabling environment for investments in agriculture sector. The project is partnering with the Department of Agriculture, the Philippines the Malaysia Bioeconomy Development Corporation, and Asia Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC).
projects.outcome: Food and nutrition systems meet the needs of all people in Malaysia, address undernutrition and obesity, specifically among women, children, and other vulnerable groups.

projects.name: Output 2.2 - Strengthening Climate Resilience through Urban Renewal and Sustainable MSME Supply Chains in Perak
projects.description:
Preparatory Assistance to formulate a project aiming to strengthen the climate resilience of Perak's urban fabric and micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) by transforming climate-vulnerable urban renewal infrastructure and MSME supply chains in Ipoh and the wider Perak region into inclusive, investment-ready, and climate-adaptive systems.
The project delivers systemic change through three integrated components: (1) Strengthening Climate Resilience of Urban Renewal Infrastructure in Ipoh; (2) Enhancing Climate Resilience of Urban MSME Value Chains in Perak; and (3) Scaling up Adaptive Capacity through Climate Finance. Together, these components integrate climate risk intelligence, nature-based solutions (NbS), capacity building, and investment-readiness pathways to safeguard livelihoods, protect ecosystems, and position Perak as a replicable model for climate-resilient urban economic transformation in Malaysia.
The project operationalizes UNIDO's FairShare Programme Theory of Change, demonstrating how green supply chains, fair value distribution, and better skills converge to deliver inclusive climate resilience across Perak's urban and MSME economy — extending beyond tourism to the broader urban services, retail, creative industries, and mixed-use enterprises that form the backbone of the city's economic ecosystem.
projects.outcome: Productivity and competitiveness, particularly of MSMEs, are enhanced as Malaysia transitions to a digital and green high-income economy with a fair and transparent business environment which promotes SDG-aligned investments

projects.name: Regional, state and non-state institutions have capacity and leadership to implement laws, policies and strategies on gender equality and women’s rights through inclusive and accountable systems including financing and data
projects.description:
The regional project, Securing Peace, Advancing Equality: Women, Peace and Security in the Indo-Pacific, is a two-year initiative to be undertaken in Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Timor Leste and Viet Nam, all of whom are notable Troop Contributing Countries (TCCs) to UN Peacekeeping operations. The project responds to the specific gaps and challenges in targeted countries, will primarily engage the Ministry of Defence, and will focus on three primary objectives:
1. Strengthen defence institutions and military forces’ understanding and operationalisation of climate-responsive WPS agenda in selected Indo-Pacific nations.
2. Promote women’s leadership and participation in defence by expanding their roles and skills in policy and expert advisory functions and equipping them to address emerging security challenges such as climate, peace and security, cybersecurity, and artificial intelligence in the context of conflict prevention.
3. Enhance civilian-military engagement to strengthen coordination, communication, and the effective use of complementary resources and expertise, particularly in context of climate impact, crisis prevention and response situations.

projects.name: Enhancing Access of Refugees to Labour Mobility Pathways through Skills Development | LM0633
projects.description: The project aims to equip refugees in Malaysia with the skills and certifications needed to access labour migration pathways out of Malaysia, directly addressing barriers such as documentation and qualifications. By mapping labour migration opportunities from Malaysia elsewhere to target destination countries, the project provides essential data to inform policies on regular pathways. Partnering with local training institutions, it will ensure that refugees receive demand-driven training and build skills aligned with labour market needs in industrial sectors abroad. Outcomes include improved access to migration pathways through enhanced refugee employability in receiving countries and increased institutional capacity to deliver skills training in Malaysia. The project contributes to SDGs 8, 9, 10, and 17 by promoting decent work, reducing inequality, and fostering cross-sector partnerships for refugee inclusion.

projects.name: Building Knowledge and Capacity on the Migration and Climate Change Nexus in South-East Asia
projects.description:
Despite ASEAN member states' capacities to respond to disasters, government action is hindered by insufficient data on climate change impacts on human mobility, lack of cross-agency collaboration, 
competing priorities, and limited expertise. These factors lead to fragmented policy efforts, complicating the regional response to climate-induced migration. The proposed Programme will contribute to the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly, and Regular Migration (GCM), including its commitments on enhancing data management, addressing migration drivers, reducing vulnerabilities, promoting skills development, and fostering international cooperation. The overall objective is to improve the climate resilience and adaptive capacity of at-risk populations, with a focus on socio-economically disadvantaged groups in selected Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) countries. IOM Malaysia focus on this project is on Outcome 1: Evidence building and Outcome 3: ASEAN Engagement
